findings.reason: the deliverable as written is under-specified — it names the count reader but not the week owner, so the implementing node would fork the weekly derivation or import a private helper, and §3 and §13 disagree on whether the figures come from velocity or are re-read.
findings.text: §13 routes the brief's "current week's four counts" through `interface_counts.count_revision_cached`, which returns counts at a revision and carries no week window; the entry that publishes a *week's* interface level — the first-parent head at the week's end, with `reckon/velocity.py:2678` already stating that its interface block exists because "the plan-review rubric reads" it — is `_interface_week_rows` (`reckon/velocity.py:2504`, `:2685`), reached through `_first_parent_head` (`:614`). §3 says the velocity view publishes the weekly figures; §13 then reads the low-level reader instead, so the composer must either re-derive the week boundary (a second composition of one display, the exact drift the recovery composer's own docstring warns against at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:515`), or reach into a private velocity helper across the module boundary — the private-name smell §6 already recorded against `plan_review._REVIEW_SIDECAR_NAME`. Name `reckon/velocity.py` as the owner of the week window (or promote a shared current-week accessor beside `_interface_week_rows`) so the reviewer is handed the same figure the velocity view publishes.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design extends two existing deep modules rather than adding one: `reckon/crew/review.py`'s rubric item set and prompt, and the plan-subject branch of `reckon/crew/recovery.py:_review_dispatch_fields` that already composes the brief behind four returned facts; no new module and no spread of wrappers over one machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the composer is told to append "the current week's four counts, read through `reckon/interface_counts.py`'s existing reader", but the current week is a derivation `reckon/velocity.py` owns and `interface_counts` has no week concept; the plan is silent on the owner.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the live design section (§13) cites the mechanism it extends, `reckon/interface_counts.py` and its reader, and the item set and prompt it grows (`reckon/crew/review.py:PLAN_DESIGN_REVIEW_ITEMS`, `reckon/crew/prompts/plan_design_review.md`); the one search it did not run is named below under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the item is not a parallel layer over an existing review; the design states its justification (the `interface_counts.py` docstring already names the plan-review rubric as its reader, so the review reads a figure the code intends it to read), and it grows the existing prompt and composer in place rather than wrapping them.
